A household electricity literacy lab · Vijeron

Understand household electricity with numbers you can check

Power labels, bills, and product ads often use different units. Everyday Energy connects them with open formulas, examples you can recalculate, and visible limits on every estimate.

Start with watts and kWh ↗Try the calculators
100 W× 10 h= 1 kWh
One number is not your whole bill

Actual costs may include tiered rates, taxes, fixed charges, and changing habits. We do not publish an automatic electricity rate that could become outdated.

01 / METHOD

Three steps you can check

01

Read a label or meter and record where the number came from.

02

Enter hours and days that match your own use.

03

Compare the estimate with billed kWh over a matching period.

02 / TOOLS

Two tools with open formulas

Calculations run in your browser. Your inputs are not sent to our server.

01 / kWh

Estimate an appliance's use

Turn watts, hours, days, and quantity into kWh. Enter your own rate if you want an estimated energy charge.

Open tool ↗
02 / Δ kWh

Compare two options

See the kWh difference between two appliances on the same schedule. Useful for lamps with comparable light output.

Open tool ↗
